national_raw_news.content: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) today approved an increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSPs), for all mandated Rabi crops for the Marketing Season 2027-28. Briefing the media in New Delhi after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the decision has been taken to ensure remunerative prices for farmers for their produce. He said the highest absolute increase in MSP has been announced for safflower at 675 rupees per quintal, followed by rapeseed and mustard at 413 rupees per quintal. The Minister said the MSP for lentil, or masur, has been increased by 390 rupees per quintal, barley by 136 rupees per quintal, gram by 83 rupees per quintal and wheat by 25 rupees per quintal. The increase in MSPs for mandated Rabi crops for the Marketing Season 2027-28 is in line with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing MSPs at a level of at least one-and-a-half times the All-India weighted average cost of production. The Minister said the CCEA has also approved the implementation of the Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) project by the Delhi Police at an estimated cost of over one thousand 789 crore rupees, inclusive of taxes. He said the project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance. Delhi has around 71 lakh active registered vehicles. Vehicular growth has substantially outpaced the expansion of road infrastructure, while traffic regulation continues to depend significantly on fixed signal timings and manual intervention. The ITMS seeks to make better use of available road capacity by enabling traffic management to respond dynamically to actual traffic conditions. Mr. Vaishnaw said the Cabinet also approved the PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) Scheme. He said the historic initiative will strengthen India’s intra-state transmission system to enable the evacuation of up to 135 gigawatts of renewable energy across States and Union Territories. The scheme also provides for the deployment of 50 gigawatt-hours of Battery Energy Storage Systems at the renewable energy developer or generator end, or at any other location of importance for grid flexibility. This will help address intermittency, congestion and peak-hour curtailment, as well as meet demand during non-solar hours. The Minister said the scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation within the States and Union Territories.

national_raw_news.content: Continuous rainfall in Nepal’s Gandak basin and Bihar has led to a record rise in the water level of the Gandak River, worsening the flood situation in North Bihar. Embankments have breached at several places, and engineers and personnel of the Water Resources Department are continuously engaged in flood-protection and relief work. Akashvani correspondent reports that, heavy rainfall in the catchment areas of the Gandak River basin in Nepal and in the districts of North Bihar has made the flood situation critical in the low-lying areas of West Champaran, East Champaran, and Gopalganj districts. The flood has now spread to Muzaffarpur, Vaishali, and Saran districts as well. More than 200 villages in these districts have been affected. In West Champaran, the Champaran embankment has breached at four places due to the strong current of the Gandak River. In Bagaha, the water level of the river has reached a new record high of 91.25 metres. In Areraj, East Champaran, the ring embankment of the Gandak has also breached. In Sheetalpur-Banjariya in Gopalganj, the Zamindari embankment broke under pressure from the Gandak River, inundating several villages. In view of the seriousness of the situation, the Water Resources Department has dispatched teams of engineers to Bagaha, Bettiah, Motihari, and Gopalganj. Meanwhile, rising water pressure in the Bagmati and Kosi rivers has affected several villages in Darbhanga, Samastipur, Supaul, and Saharsa districts. Relief and rescue operations are continuing in the affected areas. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary today conducted an aerial survey of West Champaran to assess the situation following the rise in the water level of the Gandak River. During the survey, he directed the administration to remain alert and prompt in carrying out relief and rescue operations and ensuring all necessary arrangements in the flood-affected areas.

national_raw_news.title: Punjab to be made drug-free by the end of 2029: Amit Shah 3 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: Senior BJP leader and Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that Punjab will be made drug-free by the end of 2029. Addressing a ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Rally’ in Jalandhar today, Mr. Shah said the BJP would contest the upcoming Assembly elections in Punjab on the issue of making the state free from the menace of drugs. He said the BJP fulfils the promises it makes. Mr. Shah said the government has addressed terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir and ended extremism in the North-East, adding that the focus will now be on making Punjab drug-free. Paying tribute to martyrs from Punjab, including Shaheed Bhagat Singh and Udham Singh, who played a significant role in country’s freedom struggle, Mr. Shah said the state, once known for its bravery, agriculture and prosperity, is now facing the challenge of the drug menace. He blamed Aam Aadmi Party government in the state for the deteriorating law and order situation, corruption and rising drug-related problems in Punjab. Mr. Shah said he met families affected by drug abuse who had lost their loved ones. He assured them that if the BJP comes to power in the state, those involved in selling drugs would be dealt with firmly. The Home Minister also assured farmers that their concerns will be addressed. He said efforts will also be made to revive industries and create employment opportunities for the youth in Punjab.
